items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: classical musicians, the idea of improvising was like yeah, just figure out how to play Schoenberg and Tchaikovsky and Brahms and Bach and Vivaldi

ctx.x: He’d remember it, yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

It’s like yeah, I mean all those guys. They had just colossal brain power and colossal ears and you know we’re spoiled because jazz spread through sound, through sound reproduction. And everyone said, “Oh let’s get the latest Bird album, let’s get the latest Coltrane album, let’s listen to this and figure this out.” Back then there were no albums. I mean you had to go hear someone play or get a score and study it. And that’s what all those guys did. They all studied scores and Bach, I think he walked for like two…
Yeah. He was writing chord changes.
